findings.title: Billable count does not filter out inactive projects, so customers will be overbilled
findings.explanation: The query counts every row in `projects` for the org. The neighboring `activeProjectNames` function exists because the table holds inactive rows (archived or soft-deleted), and its WHERE clause, which is not visible in this hunk, filters them out. This query drops that filter, so archived or deleted projects would be billed. Because the result feeds the invoice generator, this is a customer-facing money error. Apply the same 'active' predicate as `activeProjectNames`, ideally through a shared constant or SQL fragment so the two cannot drift apart. Then confirm with product or billing which statuses count as billable (for example, whether trial or suspended projects are included).

findings.title: No tests, and a point-in-time count may not match the billing period
findings.explanation: No tests cover the new function. Add cases for an org with active, archived, and deleted projects, and for an org with no projects. The function also returns the count at the moment it is called. If invoices cover a period, projects created or removed mid-period will be priced by when the invoice runs, not by usage during the period. Confirm that this matches the intended pricing rules, and document the semantics in the comment or function name.
